summary: This is the Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) "15Al" low-density steel in its peak-hardness state, obtained by solution treatment at 1100 °C for 10 min (argon, oil quench) followed by aging at 600 °C for 6 h and water quenching. It is the hardest condition reported in the paper for the 15Al alloy (965.6 ± 7.6 HV), and the highest Vickers hardness among all Fe-35Mn-(15,17,19)Al-5Cu alloys studied. The work systematically investigates how Al content controls the aging-hardening behavior of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels, with the aim of combining ultra-high hardness and low density through the rapid precipitation of the ultra-hard β-Mn phase.
composition: Nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%). The EDS-measured chemistry is Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 at.%, i.e. Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu. It is the lowest-Al member of the Fe-35Mn-(15,17,19)Al-5Cu series; across the series the nominal Al variation is accommodated mainly by substituting Al for Fe while Mn (~35 at.%) and Cu (~5 at.%) are held essentially constant. Design intent: the high Mn content of ~35 at.% promotes the precipitation kinetics of the hard β-Mn phase responsible for the ultra-high hardness; Cu is added (following the authors' earlier work) to promote β-Mn precipitation kinetics and raise hardness; Al is the primary density-reducing element (about 1 wt.% Al lowers density by ~0.1 g·cm⁻³) and is also the variable whose effect on β-Mn precipitation and hardening is being probed. The 15Al alloy has a measured density of 6.85 g·cm⁻³ (Archimedes method), the highest of the three alloys.
